newsitem.title: USA: Californians favor Sen Feinstein for governor-poll.
newsitem.headline: Californians favor Sen Feinstein for governor-poll.

text.p: Democratic U.S. Senator Dianne Feinstein would be strongly favored by California voters if she were to run for governor next year, according to a poll released on Tuesday.

In a simulated multiparty primary contest, where 797 registered voters were asked their preferences, Feinstein would be the leading candidate with 27 percent, followed by Republican Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan with 13 percent, according to the latest Field poll.

Republican state Attorney General Dan Lungren was preferred by 11 percent followed by former White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta, a Democrat, with 10 percent. Democratic Lt. Gov. Gray Davis stands in fifth place with just 8 percent.

If Democrats were asked to choose from only the Democratic possibilities, as would occur in a closed primary, Feinstein would lead again with 37 percent, followed by Panetta at 17 percent and Davis with 12 percent.
If Republicans were limited to choosing between Lungren and Riordan, the race would be a statistical dead heat, with Riordan preferred by 29 percent and Lungren by 28 percent.
The independent Field Institute poll was based on a survey conducted February 11-17 among a statewide sample of 388 Democrats, 321 Republicans and 88 others.
The margin of error in the survey was plus or minus 3.5 percentage points for the overall sample, 5.1 percentage points among Democrats and 6.1 percentage points among Republicans.
